extracted.intended_audience: Earth and planetary scientists, researchers, and community members interested in preprints and volunteering for EarthArXiv (Advisory Council or Community Ambassadors)
extracted.subtask_description: Announcement and call for nominations for EarthArXiv Advisory Council members and Community Ambassadors, describing roles, responsibilities, selection process, and the kinds of content EarthArXiv hosts. Intended to recruit volunteers and explain expectations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Definition of a preprint
rubrics_metrics.description: A ‘preprint’ is an as-yet, non-peer-reviewed version of a scholarly paper that precedes publication in a peer-reviewed journal.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Preprints may represent the same manuscript eventually submitted to a peer-reviewed journal; they can also be other content (e.g. datasets, method papers) that may be difficult to publish.

rubrics_metrics.name: Role of a preprint server
rubrics_metrics.description: A ‘preprint server’ ... is an online platform purpose-built to host preprints.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Preprint servers provide storage and access to scholarly content (including preprints and postprints) that would otherwise be lost, and can explicitly link preprints to associated publisher-hosted manuscripts.

rubrics_metrics.name: Acceptable content types for EarthArXiv
rubrics_metrics.description: EarthArXiv hosts preprints and can also host datasets, method papers, and postprints (published articles).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Postprints can help facilitate (Green) open access; content that is appropriate should be explicitly linked to associated manuscripts when relevant. See EarthArXiv’s moderation policy for more detail on what is and is not accepted.

rubrics_metrics.name: Moderation policy existence
rubrics_metrics.description: EarthArXiv has a moderation policy which outlines what type of material we do and do not accept.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The moderation policy (linked on the site) contains the specific accept/reject criteria and should be consulted for submission and moderation decisions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Advisory Council responsibility: moderating content
rubrics_metrics.description: Advisory Council members are primarily responsible for moderating content submitted to EarthArXiv.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Moderation implies applying the EarthArXiv moderation policy to submissions; the council will be involved in judgement calls about acceptability of materials.

rubrics_metrics.name: Advisory Council responsibility: fundraising and endorsements
rubrics_metrics.description: Advisory Council members coordinate future efforts to obtain funding and/or endorsements for EarthArXiv from professional societies.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Members should be willing/able to engage with societies and funders to secure resources or formal support for the service.

rubrics_metrics.name: Advisory Council responsibility: platform development with OSF
rubrics_metrics.description: Advisory Council members will work with OSF (Center for Open Science) to develop future functionality for EarthArXiv.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Members should be prepared to collaborate on technical/functional improvements to the server infrastructure.

rubrics_metrics.name: Advisory Council composition and continuity
rubrics_metrics.description: There are currently 15 Advisory Council members; plan is to retain services of 8 current members and add 8 new members (to serve a 2-year term), increasing the Advisory Council to 16.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Selection balances continuity with infusion of new members; terms are 2 years.

rubrics_metrics.name: Selection principle: ensure desired level of diversity
rubrics_metrics.description: After ensuring for the desired level of diversity (e.g. race, geographic, ethnic, gender, geography, area-of-interest, or any self-declared protected characteristic), a random sample of 8 members will be chosen.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Selection explicitly considers multiple diversity axes; once diversity targets are met, final selection is by random sampling among nominees.

rubrics_metrics.name: Nominations logistics and deadline
rubrics_metrics.description: If you are interested in serving, please fill out this form. Nominations will be received until October 18th at 2359.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Timeliness of nomination matters; follow the provided form link to apply before the stated deadline.

rubrics_metrics.name: Community Ambassador role: promotion
rubrics_metrics.description: Community Ambassadors are asked to promote EarthArXiv in their home institutions, communities, and countries via social media, presentations, etc.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Ambassadors can use outreach channels (social media, talks) to increase awareness and adoption of EarthArXiv.

rubrics_metrics.name: Community Ambassador role: engagement with publishers and funders
rubrics_metrics.description: Ambassadors should work with Earth science publishers and funders to accept preprints as a valid step in the publishing pipeline.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This involves advocacy and outreach to change or reinforce publisher/funder practices regarding preprints.

rubrics_metrics.name: Encouragement to evaluate repository content
rubrics_metrics.description: We strongly encourage you to visit and personally assess the quality of material available for consumption.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Members of the community are invited to inspect submissions and form their own judgements about content quality; this fosters community oversight.

rubrics_metrics.name: Contextual norms: preprints' impact on career and funding
rubrics_metrics.description: Preprints are encouraged by major funders and institutions and may inform grant review and academic advancement.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Submitting preprints can support grant applications and job applications; major publishers also encourage preprints to enhance research quality.
